title: Learning: The Ceremony
text: Some proof systems need a one-time setup. It produces public keys, and secret randomness that must not survive. Then a proof arrives that verifies perfectly.
held: Nobody was left able to forge, and the proof said what it was supposed to say.

cards.label: Publish the proving and verifying keys
Do not publish: run the setup again
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: leftover randomness
fields.value: destroyed; several independent parties took part
fields.check: Check what became of the setup's secret randomness
fields.ok: Destroyed. Several independent parties took part, and only one needed to be honest.

intrusion.detail: One participant still holds the secret randomness.
intrusion.correct: Do not publish: run the setup again
intrusion.why: Whoever holds it can forge proofs that verify. It is called toxic waste for a reason.
intrusion.reveal: One participant in the setup had kept its secret randomness.

temptations.label: Reuse a well-known project's setup: theirs was audited
temptations.why: A setup is for one circuit; theirs proves their statement, not yours. Their audit tells you nothing about keys generated for a different question.

cards.label: Reject the proof
cards.why: Nothing was wrong with it. Refusing something legitimate without looking is its own failure: check, then act.

fields.label: statement proved
fields.check: Read exactly which statement the proof is for
fields.ok: The statement is: the holder is over 18.

intrusion.detail: The proof is valid, for a different and trivial statement.
intrusion.why: It verified, and it was about something else. The verifier fixes the statement; the prover doesn't get to choose it.
intrusion.reveal: The proof was valid but proved a different statement.

teaches: Where a setup is needed, its secret leftovers must be destroyed, by people who don't all trust each other.
“It verifies” is half an answer. The other half is: verifies what?
